full_judgment:
19. D.W.2 Abdul Wahed is an employee of the defendant Board and works in the despatch section. He stated that on 4.11.93 he went to the office of M/s. M.R. Sikder at Malibagh, Dhaka and made over a letter to the office clerk of the plaintiff, who received it by putting his signature in the Peon Book against serial No.11. He asserted that the office peon of the contractor received the letter on behalf of his employer by putting his signature in the Peon Book. This entry appears at page No.198 at serial 11 of the Peon Book. It has been marked as Ext. Dha. He stated that he also carried 2 other letters to the office of M/s. M.R. Sikder on 22.11.93 and 24.11.93. These letters were also received by the plaintiffs peon Kamal by putting his signature in the Peon Book. This entry appears at page No.99 of the Peon Book of the Board. The signature of Kamal has been marked as Ext. Dha(1). 

 21. D.W.No.3 Zahirul Karim, at present Director of Training, stated that in 1993 he was the Deputy Director, Law under the BWDB. At present he looks after the arbitration cases on behalf of the Board. He stated that the Board duly intimated M/s. M.R. Sikder about the appointment of Mr. Jaigirder as the arbitrator for the Board and this letter was sent to the plaintiff through a messenger and the plaintiff company duly received the notice on 15.9.93. Thereafter the Board proceeded with the arbitration proceeding. He stated that after completing the official procedures the Board appointed Mr. G.H.A. Islam Jaigirder as the arbitrator for the Board. He went on to state that he sent a letter to the plaintiff contractor for consenting to the appointment of Mr. Jaigirder. The departmental proceeding as regards the arbitration has been marked as Ext. Na. He stated that they sent a letter on 9.11.93 to the plaintiff contractor by post as well as by a messenger. He stated that letter sent by post were duly entered in the volume of despatches as serial No.105A. The certified copy of the said entry has been marked as Ext. Pa (original replaced by certified copy). The Board also sent a copy of the said letter to the plaintiff company on 9.11.93. He signed the departmental order on 4.11.93. He asserted that the plaintiff company thereafter contacted him at his office and talked to him about the matter. He also stated that he duly informed M/s. M.R. Sikder about the appointment of Mr. Jaigirder as their arbitrator and talked to P.W.1 over the telephone, whereupon P.W.1 represented that he would receive the letter from the Board's office on his return from Chittagong. Subsequently on 9.11.93 the Board sent the letter to the plaintiff by a messenger. He asserted that the plaintiff company received on 9.11.93 the said letter of appointment of the arbitrator Mr. Jaigirder. He added that the arbitrator appointed by the Board also intimated the matter to the plaintiff company requiring the plaintiff company to take necessary steps in the matter. Mr. G.H.A. Islam Jaigirder wrote a letter to the Board, which was received on 16.11.93. In his letter Mr. Jaigirder asked the plaintiff company to submit its claims within one week. He further stated that the copies of the letters were also sent to the plaintiff company by a messenger. Office copy of the letter has been marked as Ext. Ba. He went on to state that the letters dated 22.11.93 and 23.11.93 sent by the Board to the plaintiff company were duly entered in the relevant volume of the Despatch Register. The certified copy of the relevant entry has been marked as Ext. Bha, with reference to the original letter dated 22.11.93, which was received by M/s. M.R. Sikder on 23.1.93. He further stated that the Board intimated the plaintiff company about he appointment of Mr. Jaigirder as their arbitrator orally as well as by letter. He added that by suppression of the material facts the plaintiff company fraudulently obtained the award made by. Mr. Justice Abdur Rahman Chowdhury. He stated that the award was made under mysterious circumstances and in violation of the rules and procedures. He stated that the arbitrator gave no opportunity to the Board to have its say in the matter and concluded the arbitration proceeding in unusual haste. He went on to state that they suddenly received a letter dated 29.11.93 intimating that the award was made on 29.11.93. He stated that the arbitrator misconducted himself and misconducted the proceedings. 

 22. In cross-examination he stated that the entry and the signature in the two relevant entries in the Peon Book are of the same hand. He further stated, in response to the defence query that he received on 29.11.93 a letter from Mr. Justice Abdur Rahman Chowdhury intimating them that the date of hearing of the arbitration case was on 25.11.93. All these things have been duly noted in the office register.
